title: Enterprise Information Security & Privacy Program
capability_statement: Parsons operates a full-spectrum information security and privacy program built on its company-wide Cybersecurity Practice that serves U.S. federal, state, and intelligence community customers. For inspection-program engagements, dedicated security staff are embedded within the program team and work continuously with system and network administrators on antivirus and malware controls, firewall and intrusion detection, database safeguarding, OS and hardware hardening, and protection of data in transit. The Vehicle Inspection and Compliance business line operates against SOC 2 Type 2 controls covering security, availability, and confidentiality, with quarterly security reviews and annual risk-analysis meetings led by the Senior IT Director and Information Systems Manager. Production systems are designed for AWS deployment with continuous configuration compliance via AWS Config and AWS Security Hub, automated vulnerability and code scans embedded in the deployment pipeline as enforced security gates, and centralized configuration baselines that block non-compliant components from release. Vulnerability management runs on a fixed cadence: monthly internal and quarterly external vulnerability tests, with results reviewed to enhance mitigation plans, plus security assessments triggered during and after critical system changes. The same scanning technology and methodology used for high-sensitivity U.S. government programs is applied to inspection-program infrastructure. Parsons' broader cyber posture is supported by an in-house Defense & Intelligence cyber business unit with full-spectrum offensive, defensive, and resiliency capabilities, recognition by Ethisphere as one of the World's Most Ethical Companies for 16 consecutive years through 2025, and more than 100 AWS certifications across its engineering and security workforce.

differentiators: Parsons brings a company-wide Cybersecurity Practice that supports high-sensitivity U.S. government programs and applies the same scanning technology and tradecraft to inspection-program infrastructure - a depth of capability rare among program-management vendors. Dedicated security staff are embedded directly in the program team rather than provided as a shared service, supported by network, security, and solution architects. The Vehicle Inspection and Compliance business line operates under SOC 2 Type 2 controls covering security, availability, and confidentiality, with documented quarterly security reviews and annual risk analysis. Cloud delivery is anchored by AWS Partner Solutions Provider, AWS DevOps Competency Partner, and AWS Advanced Tier Services Partner status, plus more than 100 AWS certifications in-house and an automated DevSecOps pipeline (AWS Config, AWS Security Hub, vulnerability and code-scan security gates) that blocks deployment of non-compliant components. Parsons has been the original contractor on NSA SHARKSEER since 2011 and holds Intelligence Community classified cyber contracts including a $104M vulnerability-research/reverse-engineering award and a $178M IDIQ for facility, asset, and personnel security worldwide - evidencing enterprise-grade security maturity that flows down to commercial program work. Recognition by Ethisphere as one of the World's Most Ethical Companies for 16 consecutive years through 2025 reinforces the governance posture behind the privacy and compliance program.
gap_notes: Evidence in the provided chunks supports SOC 2 Type 2 controls (Vehicle Inspection and Compliance business line) and AWS PCI-DSS Compliance Attestation referenced as a proposal attachment for the PennDOT submission. The chunks do not contain explicit Parsons-level evidence for FedRAMP, FISMA authorization, IRS-1075, CJIS, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, HIPAA, NIST 800-53/800-171 control mappings, or formal third-party penetration-test reports - these will need to be confirmed and dated by Corporate Information Security before any specific certification claim is made in a response. Specific encryption-at-rest/in-transit algorithms (e.g., AES-256, TLS 1.2/1.3) and FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated module identifiers are not stated in the provided chunks and should be sourced from the System Security Plan or equivalent control inventory before assertion. Quantified breach-notification timelines, mean-time-to-patch, and disciplinary/sanction policy specifics for security-policy violations are not present in the chunks and will require sourcing from Parsons' Information Security Policy. Threat-intelligence subscription list, ICS/SCADA/OT inventory specifics, IoT and BYOD policy details, and law-enforcement cybersecurity contact registry are not enumerated in the available evidence. The PennDOT proposal references attached SOC 2 Type II Report, AWS PCI-DSS Compliance Attestation, Security Testing Results (Redacted), and Security Incident Response Plan as separate uploaded files - these source artifacts should be retrieved to populate certification dates and scope before final response.
